narrative: OMX30 faces headwinds this morning despite remaining +6.3% above its 200-day MA. European bourses sold off sharply overnight (DAX -1.10%, CAC -1.34%) with correlation signal deeply negative at -0.734%, suggesting broad risk-off sentiment flowing northbound. The technical picture is mixed: while the index holds bull regime status, MACD has turned below signal with histogram at -4.556, and weak ADX (11.2) strips confidence from any directional move. Rising US 10Y yields (+46bp to 4.806%) create a pincer: positive for financials (NIM expansion) but negative for tech and growth names (DCF compression). Brent's 3.1% surge adds input-cost pressure to industrials and consumer discretionary, offsetting some export tailwinds from the stronger USD/SEK (+0.09%). Risk/reward tilts slightly negative.
morningBrief: Expect OMX30 to open down 0.3–0.6% tracking European weakness and yield pressure. Support sits at 3085 (lower Bollinger band), with the previous close at 3123 serving as the initial pivot. Resistance is 3180 (50-MA). Banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) should see modest support from wider NIM expectations on the 4.8% 10Y, but tech (Ericsson, Hexagon) faces NASDAQ sentiment drag (down -0.32%) and DCF compression. Industrials (Volvo, Atlas Copco) are mixed: USD/SEK strength helps exports, but oil's 3% jump eats into margins. Boliden gets a boost from gold (+0.9%) and stable copper, making it a tactical long. Watch for US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET—a surprise could reset the yield trajectory. Avoid aggressive positioning; ADX weakness and MACD divergence argue for range-trading until clarity emerges. Defensive plays (Essity, AstraZeneca) outperform in this risk-off environment.
